name: <esc>
desc: leave insert mode

name: <backspace>
desc: delete characters before cursors

name: <del>
desc: delete characters under cursors

name: <left>, <right>, <up>, <down>
desc: move the cursors in given direction

name: <home>
desc: move cursors to line begin

name: <end>
desc: move cursors to end of line

name: <c-r>
desc: insert contents of the register given by next key

name: <c-v>
desc: insert next keystroke directly into the buffer, without interpreting it

name: <c-u>
desc: commit changes up to now as a single undo group

name: <a-;>, <a-semicolon>
desc: escape to normal mode for a single command

name: <c-o>
desc: toggle automatic completion

name: <c-n>
desc: select next completion candidate

name: <c-p>
desc: select previous completion candidate

name: <c-x>
desc: explicit insert completion query, followed by:

name: <c-x> f
desc: explicit file completion

name: <c-x> w
desc: explicit word completion (current buffer)

name: <c-x> W
desc: explicit word completion (all buffers)

name: <c-x> l
desc: explicit line completion (current buffer)

name: <c-x> L
desc: explicit line completion (all buffers)

name: h
desc: select the character on the left of the end of each selection <left> maps to this by default. (See :doc mapping default-mappings)

name: j
desc: select the character below the end of each selection <down> maps to this by default. (See :doc mapping default-mappings)

name: k
desc: select the character above the end of each selection <up> maps to this by default. (See :doc mapping default-mappings)

name: l
desc: select the character on the right of the end of each selection <right> maps to this by default. (See :doc mapping default-mappings)

name: w
desc: select the word and following whitespaces on the right of the end of each selection

name: b
desc: select preceding whitespaces and the word on the left of the end of each selection

name: e
desc: select preceding whitespaces and the word on the right of the end of each selection

name: <a-[wbe]>
desc: same as [wbe] but select WORD instead of word

name: f
desc: select to the next occurrence of given character

name: t
desc: select until the next occurrence of given character

name: <a-[ft]>
desc: same as [ft] but in the other direction

name: <a-.>
desc: repeat last object or f/t selection command

name: m
desc: select to the next sequence enclosed by matching characters, see the matching_pairs option in :doc options

name: M
desc: extend the current selection to the next sequence enclosed by matching character, see the matching_pairs option in :doc options

name: <a-m>
desc: select to the previous sequence enclosed by matching characters, see the matching_pairs option in :doc options

name: <a-M>
desc: extend the current selection to the previous sequence enclosed by matching characters, see the matching_pairs option in :doc options

name: x
desc: expand selections to contain full lines (including end-of-lines)

name: <a-x>
desc: trim selections to only contain full lines (not including last end-of-line)

name: %, <percent>
desc: select whole buffer

name: <a-h>
desc: select to line begin <home> maps to this by default. (See :doc mapping default-mappings)

name: <a-l>
desc: select to line end <end> maps to this by default. (See :doc mapping default-mappings)

name: <c-u>
desc: scroll half a page up

name: <c-d>
desc: scroll half a page down

name: ;, <semicolon>
desc: reduce selections to their cursor

name: <a-;>, <a-semicolon>
desc: flip the direction of each selection

name: <a-:>
desc: ensure selections are in forward direction (cursor after anchor)

name: i
desc: enter insert mode before selections

name: a
desc: enter insert mode after selections

name: d
desc: yank and delete selections

name: c
desc: yank and delete selections and enter insert mode
repeat last insert mode change (i, a, or c, including the inserted text)

name: <a-d>
desc: delete selections (not yanking)

name: <a-c>
desc: delete selections and enter insert mode (not yanking)

name: I
desc: enter insert mode at the beginning of the lines containing the start of each selection

name: A
desc: enter insert mode at the end of the lines containing the end of each selection

name: o
desc: enter insert mode in a new line (or in a given count of new lines) below the end of each selection

name: O
desc: enter insert mode in a new line (or in a given count of new lines) above the beginning of each selection

name: <a-o>
desc: add an empty line below cursor

name: <a-O>
desc: add an empty line above cursor

name: y
desc: yank selections

name: p
desc: paste after the end of each selection

name: P
desc: paste before the beginning of each selection

name: <a-p>
desc: paste all after the end of each selection, and select each pasted string

name: <a-P>
desc: paste all before the start of each selection, and select each pasted string

name: R
desc: replace selections with yanked text

name: <a-R>
desc: replace selections with every yanked text

name: r
desc: replace each character with the next entered one

name: <a-j>
desc: join selected lines

name: <a-J>
desc: join selected lines and select spaces inserted in place of line breaks

name: <a-_>
desc: merge contiguous selections together (works across lines as well)

name: <+>, <plus>
desc: duplicate each selection (generating overlapping selections)

name: <a-+>, <a-plus>
desc: merge overlapping selections

name: >, <gt>
desc: indent selected lines

name: <a-\>>, <a-gt>
desc: indent selected lines, including empty lines

name: <, <lt>
desc: unindent selected lines

name: <a-<>, <a-lt>
desc: unindent selected lines, do not remove incomplete indent (3 leading spaces when indent is 4)

name: u
desc: undo last change

name: U
desc: redo last change

name: <c-j>
desc: move forward in changes history

name: <c-k>
desc: move backward in changes history

name: <a-u>
desc: undo last selection change

name: <a-U>
desc: redo last selection change
align selections, align the cursor of each selection by inserting spaces before the first character of each selection

name: <a-&>
desc: copy indent, copy the indentation of the main selection (or the count one if a count is given) to all other ones
to lower case
to upper case

name: <a-`>
desc: swap case
convert tabs to spaces in each selection, uses the buffer tabstop option or the count parameter for tabstop

name: <a-@>
desc: convert spaces to tabs in each selection, uses the buffer tabstop option or the count parameter for tabstop
unselect whitespace surrounding each selection, drop those that only contain whitespace

name: <a-)>
desc: rotate selections content, if specified, the count groups selections, so the following command

name: <a-(>
desc: rotate selections content backward
pipe each selection through the given external filter program and replace the selection with its output.

name: <a-|>
desc: pipe each selection through the given external filter program and ignore its output.
insert and select command output before each selection.

name: <a-!>
desc: append and select command output after each selection.
select next match after each selection

name: <a-/>
desc: select previous match before each selection
extend to next match after each selection

name: <a-?>
desc: extend to previous match before each selection

name: n
desc: select next match after the main selection

name: N
desc: add a new selection with next match after the main selection

name: <a-n>
desc: select previous match before the main selection

name: <a-N>
desc: add a new selection with previous match before the main selection

name: <a- *>
desc: set the search pattern to the main selection (verbatim, no smart detection)

name: g, G
desc: When a count is specified, G only extends the selection to the given line, g sends the anchor to the given line and a menu is then displayed which waits for one of the following additional keys:

name: g h
desc: go to line begin

name: g l
desc: go to line end

name: g i
desc: go to non blank line start

name: g g, g k
desc: go to the first line

name: g j
desc: go to the last line

name: g e
desc: go to last char of last line

name: g t
desc: go to the first displayed line

name: g c
desc: go to the middle displayed line

name: g b
desc: go to the last displayed line

name: g a
desc: go to the previous (alternate) buffer

name: g f
desc: open the file whose name is selected

name: g .
desc: go to last buffer modification position

name: v, V
desc: V enters lock view mode (which will be left when the <esc> is hit), and v modifies the current view; a menu is then displayed which waits for one of the following additional keys:

name: v v, v c
desc: center the main selection in the window (vertically)

name: v m
desc: center the main selection in the window (horizontally)

name: v t
desc: scroll to put the main selection on the top line of the window

name: v b
desc: scroll to put the main selection on the bottom line of the window

name: v <
desc: scroll to put the main cursor on the leftmost column of the window

name: v >
desc: scroll to put the main cursor on the rightmost column of the window

name: v h
desc: scroll the window count columns left

name: v j
desc: scroll the window count line downward

name: v k
desc: scroll the window count line upward

name: v l
desc: scroll the window count columns right

name: Z
desc: save selections to the register

name: z
desc: restore selections from the register

name: <a-z>, <a-Z>
desc: <a-z> combines selections from the register with the current ones, whereas <a-Z> combines current selections with the ones in the register; a menu is then displayed which waits for one of the following additional keys:

name: <a-z> a
desc: append selections

name: <a-z> u
desc: keep a union of selections

name: <a-z> i
desc: keep an intersection of selections

name: <a-z> <
desc: select the selection with the leftmost cursor for each pair

name: <a-z> >
desc: select the selection with the rightmost cursor for each pair

name: <a-z> +
desc: select the longest selection

name: <a-z> -
desc: select the shortest selection

name: Q
desc: start or end macro recording

name: q
desc: play a recorded macro

name: <c-i>
desc: jump forward

name: <c-o>
desc: jump backward

name: <c-s>
desc: create a jump step, but also save the current selection to have it be restored when the step is subsequently cycled through

name: s
desc: create a selection for each match of the given regex (selects the count capture if it is given)

name: S
desc: split selections with the given regex (selects the count capture if it is given)

name: <a-s>
desc: split selections on line boundaries

name: <a-S>
desc: select first and last characters of each selection

name: C
desc: duplicate selections on the lines that follow them

name: <a-C>
desc: duplicate selections on the lines that precede them

name: <a-k>
desc: keep selections that match the given regex

name: <a-K>
desc: clear selections that match the given regex
pipe each selection to the given shell command and keep the ones for which the shell returned 0. Shell expansions are available, (See :doc expansions shell-expansions)
rotate main selection (the main selection becomes the next one)
rotate main selection backward (the main selection becomes the previous one)

name: <a-a>
desc: select the whole surrounding object
select to the whole surrounding object start
select to the whole surrounding object end
extend selections to the whole surrounding object start
extend selections to the whole surrounding object end

name: <a-i>
desc: select the surrounding inner object

name: <a-[>
desc: select to the surrounding inner object start

name: <a-]>
desc: select to the surrounding inner object end

name: <a-{>
desc: extend selections to the surrounding inner object start

name: <a-}>
desc: extend selections to the surrounding inner object end

name: <a-I>
desc: select each inner nested object in selections

name: b, (, )
desc: select the enclosing parenthesis

name: B, {, }
desc: select the enclosing {} block

name: r, [, ]
desc: select the enclosing [] block

name: a, <, >
desc: select the enclosing <> block

name: Q, "
desc: select the enclosing double quoted string

name: q, '
desc: select the enclosing single quoted string

name: g, `
desc: select the enclosing grave quoted string

name: w
desc: select the whole word

name: <a-w>
desc: select the whole WORD

name: s
desc: select the sentence

name: p
desc: select the paragraph
select the whitespaces

name: i
desc: select the current indentation block

name: n
desc: select the number

name: u
desc: select the argument

name: c
desc: select user defined object, will prompt for open and close text

name: <a-;>, <a-semicolon>
desc: run a command with additional expansions describing the selection context (See :doc expansions)

name: <ret>
desc: validate prompt

name: <esc>
desc: abandon without validating prompt

name: <left>, <c-b>
desc: move cursor to previous character

name: <right>, <c-f>
desc: move cursor to next character

name: <home>, <c-a>
desc: move cursor to first character

name: <end>, <c-e>
desc: move cursor past the last character

name: <backspace>, <c-h>
desc: erase character before cursor

name: <del>, <c-d>
desc: erase character under cursor

name: <a-f>
desc: advance to next word begin

name: <a-F>
desc: advance to next WORD begin

name: <a-b>
desc: go back to previous word begin

name: <a-B>
desc: go back to previous WORD begin

name: <a-e>
desc: advance to next word end

name: <a-E>
desc: advance to next WORD end

name: <c-w>
desc: erase to previous word begin, save erased content to clipboard

name: <c-W>
desc: erase to previous WORD begin, save erased content to clipboard

name: <a-d>
desc: erase to next word begin, save erased content to clipboard

name: <a-D>
desc: erase to next WORD begin, save erased content to clipboard

name: <c-k>
desc: erase to end of line, save erased content to clipboard

name: <c-u>
desc: erase to begin of line, save erased content to clipboard

name: <c-y>
desc: insert clipboard content before cursor

name: <up>, <c-p>
desc: select previous entry in history

name: <down>, <c-n>
desc: select next entry in history

name: <tab>
desc: select next completion candidate

name: <s-tab>
desc: select previous completion candidate

name: <c-r>
desc: insert the content of the register given by next key, if next key has the Alt modifier, it will insert all values in the register joined with spaces, else it will insert the main one. if it has the Control modifier, it will quote the inserted value(s).

name: <c-v>
desc: insert next keystroke without interpreting it

name: <c-x>
desc: explicit completion query, followed by:

name: <c-x> f
desc: explicit file completion

name: <c-x> w
desc: explicit word completion (from current buffer)

name: <c-o>
desc: toggle automatic completion

name: <a-!>
desc: expand the typed expansions in currently entered text (See :doc expansions)

name: <a-;>, <a-semicolon>
desc: escape to normal mode for a single command

name: <space>
desc: enter default user mode to access custom commands (See :doc modes user-mode)

name: <c-c>
desc: Stop any external processes. If you ever see Kakoune display a message like "waiting for shell command to finish", this key will stop that command so you can regain control of Kakoune. Technically, this key causes Kakoune to send the SIGINT signal to its entire process group.

name: <c-g>
desc: Cancel a long-running Kakoune operation, such as a regex search on a very large file. This also clears Kakoune's input buffer, so any commands that were waiting for the long-running operation to complete will also be cancelled.

name: doc <topic>
desc: alias help + display documentation about a topic. The completion list displays the available topics

name: arrange-buffers <buffer>...
desc: Reorder the buffers in the buffers list. The named buffers will be moved to the front of the buffer list, in the order given. Buffers that do not appear in the parameters will remain at the end of the list, keeping their current order.

name: arrange-buffers -back
desc: Move the named buffers to the back, rather than the fron, of the buffer list..

name: change-directory [<directory>]
desc: alias cd + change the current directory to directory, or the home directory if unspecified

name: edit[!] [<switches>] <filename> [<line> [<column>]]
desc: alias e + open buffer on file, go to given line and column. If file is already opened, just switch to this file. Use edit! to force reloading

name: edit[!] -debug
desc: The new buffer (if any) will be created as a debug buffer. (See :doc buffers debug-buffers)

name: edit[!] -existing
desc: If the named file does not exist, fail instead of creating a new buffer.

name: edit[!] -readonly
desc: The new buffer (if any) will be set read-only.

name: edit[!] -fifo <fifoname>
desc: Creates a new scratch buffer named <filename>, and continually appends data from the fifo (named pipe) <fifoname> as it arrives. (See :doc buffers fifo-buffers)

name: edit[!] -scratch
desc: Creates a new buffer named <filename>, which doesn't correspond to any file on disk. If no filename is given, the buffer name will be generated based on format \scratch-$ID, where $ID is an integer automatically incremented for new buffers. (See :doc buffers scratch-buffers)

name: edit[!] -scroll
desc: If used with -fifo, when new data arrives Kakoune will scroll the buffer down to make the new data visible. Otherwise, does nothing.

name: write[!] [-force] [-sync] [-method <writemethod>] [<filename>]
desc: alias w + write buffer to <filename> or use its name if filename is not given. If the file is write-protected, its permissions are temporarily changed to allow saving the buffer and restored afterwards when the write! command is used.

name: write[!] -force
desc: Equivalent to !, allow overwiting existing files if <filename> is given and set permissions temporarily if necessary.

name: write[!] -sync
desc: Synchronise the filesystem after the write

name: write[!] -method <writemethod>
desc: Enforce write method instead of relying on the writemethod option

name: write-all [-sync] [-method <writemethod>]
desc: alias wa + write all changed buffers that are associated with a file

name: quit[!] [<exit status>]
desc: alias q + exit Kakoune, use quit! to force quitting even if there is some unsaved buffer remaining. If specified, the client exit status will be set to <exit status>

name: write-quit[!] [-sync] [-method <writemethod>] [<exit status>]
desc: alias wq + write current buffer and quit current client. If specified, the client exit status will be set to <exit status>

name: write-all-quit [-sync] [-method <writemethod>] [<exit status>]
desc: alias waq + write all buffers and quit. If specified, the client exit status will be set to <exit status>

name: buffer <name>
desc: alias b + switch to buffer <name>

name: buffer-next
desc: alias bn + switch to the next buffer. Debug buffers are skipped. (See :doc buffers debug-buffers)

name: buffer-previous
desc: alias bp + switch to the previous buffer. Debug buffers are skipped. (See :doc buffers debug-buffers)

name: delete-buffer[!] [<name>]
desc: alias db + delete current buffer or the buffer <name> if specified

name: rename-buffer [-file|-scratch] <name>
desc: set current buffer name, if -scratch or -file is given, ensure the buffer is set to the corresponding type.

name: source <filename> <param>...
desc: execute commands in <filename> parameters are available in the sourced script as %arg{0}, %arg{1}, …

name: rename-client <name>
desc: set current client name Client names may only contain letters, numbers, -, and _.

name: rename-session <name>
desc: set current session name

name: kill[!] [<exit status>]
desc: terminate the current session, all the clients as well as the server. If specified, the server and clients exit status will be set to <exit status>

name: declare-option [<switches>] <type> <name> [<value>]
desc: alias decl + declare a new option, the -hidden switch hides the option in completion suggestions (See :doc options declare-option)

name: set-option [<switches>] <scope> <name> <value>
desc: alias set + change the value of an option in scope (See :doc options set-option and :doc scopes)

name: unset-option <scope> <name>
desc: alias unset + unset the value of an option in scope, so the value from an outer scope is used (See :doc options unset-option and :doc scopes)

name: update-option <scope> <name>
desc: update the value of an option if its type supports that operation (See :doc options update-option and :doc scopes)

name: define-command [<switches>] <name> <command>
desc: alias def + define a new command (See Declaring new commands)

name: alias <scope> <name> <command>
desc: define a new alias named name in scope (See Using aliases and :doc scopes)

name: complete-command [<switches>] <name> <type> [<param>]
desc: alias compl + configure how a command completion works (See Configuring command completion)

name: unalias <scope> <name> [<command>]
desc: remove an alias if its current value is the same as the one passed as an optional parameter, remove it unconditionally otherwise (See Using aliases and :doc scopes)

name: evaluate-commands [<switches>] <command> ...
desc: alias eval + evaluate commands, as if they were entered in the command prompt (See :doc execeval)

name: execute-keys [<switches>] <key> ...
desc: alias exec + execute a series of keys, as if they were hit (See :doc execeval)

name: map [<switches>] <scope> <mode> <key> <keys>
desc: bind a list of keys to a combination (See :doc mapping and :doc scopes)

name: unmap <scope> <mode> <key> [<expected>]
desc: unbind a key combination (See :doc mapping and :doc scopes)

name: declare-user-mode <name>
desc: declare a new user keymap mode

name: enter-user-mode [<switches>] <name>
desc: enable <name> keymap mode for next key

name: enter-user-mode -lock
desc: stay in mode until <esc> is pressed

name: enter-user-mode -count <count>
desc: Forward count to the underlying normal mode parameters

name: enter-user-mode -register <register>
desc: Forward register to the underlying normal mode parameters

name: hook [<switches>] <scope> <hook_name> <filtering_regex> <command>
desc: execute command whenever a hook_name is triggered in scope (See :doc hooks and :doc scopes)

name: hook -group <groupname>
desc: Add this hook to the groupname group, so it can be removed by the remove-hooks command (below) or disabled with the disabled_hooks option (see :doc options builtin-options).

name: hook -once
desc: This hook will be automatically removed after it has been executed.

name: hook -always
desc: This hook will run even while hooks are disabled. See :doc hooks disabling-hooks.

name: remove-hooks <scope> <group>
desc: alias rmhooks + remove every hook in scope whose group matches the regex group (See :doc hooks and :doc scopes)

name: trigger-user-hook <param>
desc: trigger the User hook with the given param as filter string in the current context. (See :doc hooks)

name: echo [<switches>] <text>
desc: show text in status line, with the following switches:

name: echo -markup
desc: expand the markup strings in text (See :doc faces markup-strings)

name: echo -debug
desc: print the given text to the \debug buffer

name: echo -to-file <filename>
desc: write the given text to the given file on the host filesystem.

name: echo -to-shell-script <script>
desc: execute the given shell script with the given text written to its standard input

name: echo -quoting <quoting>
desc: define how arguments are quoted in echo output:

name: set-face <scope> <name> <facespec>
desc: alias face + define a face in scope (See :doc faces and :doc scopes)

name: unset-face <scope> <name>
desc: Remove a face definition from scope (See :doc faces and :doc scopes)

name: colorscheme <name>
desc: load named colorscheme + Colorschemes are just .kak scripts that set faces. Colorschemes are searched for in %val{config}/colors and %val{runtime}/colors. + (See :doc faces and :doc expansions)

name: add-highlighter [<switches>] <highlighter_path> <highlighter_parameters> ...
desc: alias addhl + add a highlighter to the current window (See :doc highlighters)

name: remove-highlighter <highlighter_path>
desc: alias rmhl + remove the highlighter whose id is highlighter_id (See :doc highlighters)

name: prompt [<switches>] <prompt> <command>
desc: prompt the user for a string, when the user validates, executes the command. The entered text is available in the text value accessible through $kak_text in shells or %val{text} in commands.

name: on-key <command>
desc: wait for next key from user, then execute <command>, the key is available through the key value, accessible through $kak_key in shells, or %val{key} in commands.

name: info [<switches>] <text>
desc: display text in an information box with the following switches:

name: info -anchor <line>.<column>
desc: print the text at the given coordinates

name: info -style <style>
desc: set the style and placement of the message box.

name: menu
desc: display the info next to the displayed menu, as documentation for the currently selected entry.

name: above
desc: display the info above the given anchor

name: below
desc: display the info below the given anchor

name: modal
desc: display the info modally, and do not auto-close the info or replace it with non modal info boxes. To hide a modal info box, use info -style modal with no arguments.

name: info -title <text>
desc: set the title of the message box

name: info -markup
desc: parse markup in both title (if provided) and text. (See :doc faces markup-strings)

name: try <commands> [catch <on_error_commands>]...
desc: prevent an error in commands from aborting the whole command execution, execute on_error_commands instead. If nothing is to be done on error, the catch part can be omitted. If an error is raised in the on_error_commands, that error is propagated, except if another catch and on_error_commands parameter follows, in which case those commands get executed, and so-on. During error commands, the description of the last raised error is available as $kak_error in the shell, or %val{error} in commands.

name: nop
desc: does nothing, but arguments will be evaluated (e.g. shell expansion)

name: fail <text>
desc: raise an error, uses <text> as its description

name: set-register <name> <contents>...
desc: alias reg + set register name to content, each content parameter is assigned to a different string in the register. (See :doc registers)

name: select [<switches>] <anchor_line>.<anchor_column>,<cursor_line>.<cursor_column>...
desc: replace the current selections with the ones described in the arguments

name: select -timestamp <timestamp>
desc: specify which buffer timestamp those coordinates apply to. Uses current buffer timestamp if not specified.

name: -codepoint
desc: provided columns are to be interpreted as codepoint counts, not byte counts.

name: -display-column
desc: provided columns are to be interpreted as display column counts, not byte counts.

name: debug {info,buffers,options,memory,shared-strings,profile-hash-maps,faces,mappings}
desc: print some debug information in the \debug buffer

name: provide-module [<switches>] <name> <commands>
desc: declares a module name that is defined by commands. commands will be evaluated as if by source the first time require-module <name> is run.

name: provide-module -override
desc: allow the module to replace an existing one with the same name. Fails if the module has already been evaluated.

name: require-module <name>
desc: guarantees the commands associated with name have been evaluated before continuing command execution. Fails if name has not been defined by a provide-module command. Does nothing if the associated commands have already been evaluated.

name: define-command [<switches>] <command_name> <commands>
desc: commands is a string containing the commands to execute, and switches can be any combination of the following parameters:

name: define-command -params <num>
desc: the command accepts a num parameter, which can be either a number, or of the form <min>..<max>, with both <min> and <max> omittable

name: define-command -override

name: complete-command shell-script
desc: following string is a shell command which takes parameters as positional params and outputs one completion candidate per line. The provided shell command will run after each keypress. During the execution of the shell command, the following env vars are available:

name: $kak_token_to_complete
desc: Index of the token being completed in the command line. Note that unlike the Unix argv tradition, 0 is the first argument, not the command name itself.

name: $kak_pos_in_token
desc: Position of the cursor inside the token being completed, in bytes from token start.

name: complete-command shell-script-candidates
desc: following string is a shell script which takes parameters as positional params and outputs one completion candidate per line. The provided shell script will run once at the beginning of each completion session, candidates are cached and then used by kakoune internal fuzzy engine.
